title: Fix misattribution and double-counting from rate-limit retries and edge batching
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Production telemetry shows a persistent discrepancy in per-model token and request counts surfaced in Console charts between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-02. Investigation indicates two related root causes: (1) the edge rate-limiter performs retries on transient throttles and the retry path does not propagate the original request_id and model_id reliably; (2) the edge batching service (continuous-batcher) will merge inflight requests into batches and emit usage events for both the original attempt and the retried attempt in certain timing windows. The combination leads to: (A) a non-trivial number of tokens attributed to a generic 'unknown' or 'null' model bucket in per-model breakdowns, and (B) double-counted tokens/requests when both the original and retry ingestion arrive and are accepted by the metrics pipeline.

Why this matters:
- Console per-model charts and token billing windows are becoming inconsistent with raw request logs for affected customers.
- Billing reconciliation queries for committed Dedicated customers are failing acceptance thresholds for accuracy (variances >1.5% for some high-volume clients).
- This affects rate-limit quota enforcement dashboards (requests appear to be consumed twice during transient throttles), leading to confusing UX and possible erroneous quota exhaustion alerts.

Repro (local / labs):
1) Run edge-proxy with rate-limiter in strict mode and inject short 50ms added latency in the batching layer.
2) Send 200 small streaming requests targeting model-id "meta-open-7b" at a burst rate that triggers a single retry for ~10% attempts.
3) Observe metrics emitted to the ingestion pipeline: some events arrive with request_id null or new UUIDs, some duplicate with same token counts.
4) Run the current dedupe job; it catches ~40% of duplicates but misses those where the model_id is missing.

Initial hypothesis and root cause details:
- Rate-limiter retry flow issues: when the limiter responds with 429 and the edge performs an automated retry, the header X-Original-Request-Id was not consistently forwarded through the batching codepath. The retry gets a new request_id and sometimes loses model_id metadata if the client-side model selection happened earlier in the pipeline.
- Batcher emission semantics: continuous-batcher emits per-batch usage documents at flush time. If a retry arrives before the original batch flush completes, both attempts can be merged and cause two usage events to be written when flush/dedup ordering races with ingestion ordering.
- Metrics pipeline currently deduplicates by request_id only; missing request_id leads to both events being accepted.

Scope and constraints:
- Affected window is estimated 2026-02-25..2026-03-02 across hosted API frontends in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 during a capacity spike.
- Volume: ~1.2M affected request events, ~3.4M tokens potentially misattributed (approx 0.7% of daily token vol during peak).
- Production fix must be low-risk and backwards compatible with Dedicated/private deployments that have different edge proxies.
acceptance_criteria: All ingested usage events in a 72h window after the fix must have either original_request_id or retry_parent_id populated for >99.9% of cases.
Per-model token counts in Console for previously affected customers must realign to within 0.2% of raw request logs after running the dedupe-backfill job.
No increase in API tail latency (>1ms p99 delta) after change in edge headers propagation and batching behavior.
Automated end-to-end test added that simulates a retry + batch merge and asserts dedupe logic prevents double-counting.
plan: Add guaranteed propagation of X-Original-Request-Id and X-Model-Id headers across the edge -> rate-limiter -> batching path (edge-proxy change).

Modify continuous-batcher to attach a transient 'retry_parent_id' when it sees events with X-Original-Request-Id present, and ensure emitted usage docs include both request_id and retry_parent_id fields.

Enhance ingestion dedupe service to consider (request_id, retry_parent_id, client_request_signature) tuple when deciding duplicates; treat null model_id specially by falling back to client_request_signature hashing.
Deploy edge-proxy change to a single canary region (us-west-2) and run synthetic bursts for 48h to validate no regression in latency.

Run a scoped backfill/dedupe job for the 2026-02-25..2026-03-02 window with conservative dedupe thresholds, produce a preview and notify affected customers; then apply corrected records to the Console timeseries store.
testing_plan: Unit tests for header propagation in edge-proxy and for continuous-batcher emission fields.
Integration test in staging that replays recorded 429-retry traces and asserts single accepted usage event per logical request.
Perf test: measure p50/p95/p99 of request path before/after change in staging with 50K req/s sustained for 1hr.
Backfill dry-run: produce pre/post snapshot diffs for per-model charts and run reconciliation script to ensure alignment within acceptance criteria.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge edge header propagation + batching changes behind feature flag GH-FF/20247; deploy to canary us-west-2 with feature flag off by default.
Phase 2: Enable feature flag for internal traffic and synthetic test clients for 24h. If stable, enable for 10% of production traffic for 48h.
Phase 3: If no regressions, ramp to 100% in the region and then roll to eu-west-1. Dedicated/private customers get the change as a patch release note and opt-in config for older proxies.
Phase 4: Run dedupe-backfill job for the affected window. Start with preview reporting to Customer Success and legal for review before applying to billing/console.
monitoring: Create dashboard: 'Retry Attribution — ENG-20247' tracking fraction of usage events with null model_id, duplicate request_id detections, per-region duplicate rate, and ingestion-latency distribution.
Alert: duplicate-rate > 0.05% for 10m -> P1 paging to oncall infra-team.
Post-rollout runbook entry for handling backfill mismatches and customer inquiries (Confluence link in links).

2026-03-05 — Priya Nair (Observability): Added a temporary dashboard that surfaces request_id coverage and duplication rate; early numbers show ~0.9% of events missing request_id in affected regions.
2026-03-07 — Rohit Singh: Pushed PR for continuous-batcher to include retry_parent_id and started unit tests. Related PR: platform/pull/13456. Putting changes behind FF-GH-20247.

2026-03-09 — QA: Performed integration replay test — dedupe logic now catches 96% of synthetic duplicates; remaining misses are where both request_id and original headers were lost upstream. Planning fallback hashing approach next.
